event_note: Not confirmed from a company source: no Lakeland Financial release or IR notice for the Q3 2026 date was found. EDGAR (CIK 721994) shows no pre-announcement 8-K. The latest filing is the 2026-10-13 dividend 8-K, items 7.01/9.01, which names no earnings date, and the investors.lakecitybank.com site returned 403. The company has not pre-announced its print dates in 2026 either: the 07-14 and 04-14 8-Ks were dividends only. Three aggregators agree on Mon 2026-10-26 before the open at 7:00 a.m. ET: Earnings Whispers, MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-lakeland-financial-lkfn-expected-to-announce-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/) and Simply Wall St. The 91-day cadence fits exactly (Q2 2026-07-27, Q3 2025 2025-10-27). The prior 8-K item 2.02 filings were accepted around 11:00 ET on the release day, so the reaction falls in the 10-26 session either way. Hunted as probable-but-unconfirmed.
conviction_note: The fundamental read is a modest EPS beat. Q2 2026 diluted EPS was $1.13 on a $1.7M provision. The Q3 consensus of $1.09 sits below that run-rate, and Indiana and Midwest peers that have reported Q3 2026 show NIM up 4-6bp quarter on quarter. That gives print_vs_bar +3.7%. The reaction lean is smaller: p_up 58 on abs 3.5 gives +0.56. The reasons are a mixed reaction history (the Q3 2025 $0.01 beat fell 5.1%), a credit tail from the rising individually-analyzed book, and the inference-based nature of the beat. The findings sum to +1.30 and the scaled number is +0.56. The gap is the sign uncertainty, which sits in p_up rather than shrinking the findings. The event itself is only aggregator-confirmed.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS $1.09 consensus, from 4 analysts. Three agreeing sources: MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-lakeland-financial-lkfn-expected-to-announce-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/), Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/LKFN) and Tickflow/AAII. The revenue bar is $72.2-74.0M (sources disagree slightly) against Q2 total revenue of $70.9M. LKFN gives no numeric guidance, so there is no company guide. The EPS bar is sourced; the revenue bar is loosely sourced, and revenue misses have not been punished (Q2: revenue missed $72.1M, stock +3.67%).
positioning_check: Short interest per FINRA data via equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/lkfn/shortinterest): 2,484,880 shares at settlement 2026-09-30, 11.0 days to cover. It has risen for five straight settlements, from 2,173,782 on 07-31, and the 10-15 estimate is about 2.46M. That is about 10.0% of the 24,857,840 shares outstanding (10-Q cover, 2026-07-29). This is a crowded short for a regional bank. There is no usable option chain (ATM spread 92% of mid, OI 15), so there is no skew. The tape: 20-day run-up -1.23%, 7.7% off the 52-week high, 6.8% above the 52-week low. Ratings average Hold (1 Buy, 3 Hold) with a $66.50 target against $58.78 spot.

findings.finding: The Q3 2026 consensus EPS of $1.09 sits $0.04 below Q2 2026's reported $1.13 diluted EPS. Q2 net income was $28.4M on NII $58.3M, NIM 3.49%, provision $1.7M and NCOs of $24k. Loans grew $106M (+2%) linked quarter and management guided to keep funding loan growth from about $51.9M of securities cash flows. A flat quarter on the Q2 run-rate (about $1.12-1.16 with provision at $2-3M) clears the bar. The street is effectively modelling a sequential EPS decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats of $0.05 in Q2 2026 (+3.67%), Q1 2026 (+3.12%) and Q4 2025 (+4.20%) were bought. The Q3 2025 $0.01 beat ($1.03 vs $1.02, per Zacks) fell 5.14%, with linked-quarter net income down 2%. 5 of the last 7 prints were up.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has been persistently conservative: beats of $0.05, $0.01 and $0.05 in the last three quarters. The FY $4.37 estimate leaves only about $2.20 for H2, so the low quarterly bar is mechanical rather than a stated concern. If the market already priced a beat, the stock would not be sitting 6.8% above its 52-week low with a Hold consensus and short interest building into the print.
findings.independence: Peer NIM expansion in Q3 2026 points the same way (separate finding, separate source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000712534/000071253426000073/a3q26earningsreleaseex991.htm). Consensus figure: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-lakeland-financial-lkfn-expected-to-announce-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/

findings.finding: Indiana and Midwest peers that reported Q3 2026 after LKFN last spoke expanded NIM sequentially. First Merchants (Indiana, 10-21) reported 3.44% FTE, +6bp q/q, above its own 3.38-3.40% H2 plan; adjusted EPS was $1.10 vs $1.06 consensus. 1st Source (South Bend) reported 4.28%, +4bp on stable deposit costs. Old National called credit stable (NCO 27bp vs 26bp). A sequential NIM gain at LKFN from its 3.49% (CFO: close to the 3.50% peak; the steepening curve helps) would push NII above the run-rate the bar implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM: in Q3 2025 NIM peaked at 3.50%, yet net income fell q/q and the stock fell 5.1%. In Q2 2026 NIM was flat at 3.49% while NII grew 3% and the stock rose 3.7%. The stock has followed EPS and NII growth more than the NIM print itself.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer prints from 10-21 are only two sessions old. The LKFN consensus ($1.09, revenue around $72-74M) does not visibly reflect them, because the estimate count is 4 and the EPS number sits below the last quarter. If the market had carried the peer read across, the LKFN estimate would have moved up after 10-21. All sources show it at the same $1.09 since at least 10-19.
findings.independence: This is a proxy: no LKFN number. 1st Source Q3 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000034782/000003478226000054/ex09302026991pressrelease1.htm) and Old National 3Q26 release (https://s205.q4cdn.com/951534337/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/ONB-3Q26-Earnings-Release.pdf) are independent of the First Merchants document.

findings.finding: Short interest stood at 2,484,880 shares (about 10.0% of the 24.86M shares outstanding) at settlement 2026-09-30, or 11.0 days to cover. It has risen for five consecutive settlements, from 2.17M on 07-31. That is a crowded short for a $1.5bn Indiana bank, and on a clean beat covering pressure adds to the move.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print sourced specifically to short covering. The three beats bought +3.1% to +4.2% came with short interest around 2.0-2.2M; it is higher now.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public but carries no direction until the print does. A building short is itself a bet that credit or margin disappoints, so if the print is clean, the 11 days of cover is a mechanism the price has not yet paid out.
findings.independence: An earlier reading (2.0M shares, 6.54 DTC at 2026-06-30, from a different tracker) shows the build. Search snapshot only, no separate fetchable URL. Otherwise none.

findings.finding: Credit migration is the left tail. At 2026-06-30 the watch list plus individually analyzed loans were $198.0M (3.55% of loans), up 22bp q/q and +$15.7M. Individually analyzed loans rose to $66.9M from $43.2M after three unrelated relationships totaling $24.7M were moved in. One previously disclosed credit produced a $28.9M charge-off in Q2 2025. Management said mid-year reviews found 'no significant credit concerns'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2025, the $28.9M NCO quarter: baseline -2.00% on 2025-04-25 was Q1; Q2 2025 (2025-07-25) +2.74%, since the charge-off had been reserved. The credit-improvement prints in 2026 were bought.
findings.why_not_priced: The migration is public, but the consensus EPS of $1.09 implies only about $1.5M more provision than Q2, so a specific reserve on the $66.9M individually-analyzed book would breach the bar. The rising short interest is consistent with some holders positioning for exactly this, so it is partly priced. Shrunk for the crowded short (lesson 7).
findings.independence: Peer credit is mixed. First Merchants took a $29.4M NCO on two credits it had reserved in Q2 and classified loans rose to $420M, while Old National called credit stable. Both are proxies (https://finsee.ai/earnings/frme/2026/q3/en/).

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the federal funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, 12-0, and longer rates rose in Q3 (First Merchants cites securities valuation declines 'due to rising interest rates'). For LKFN this means a small lift to floating-rate C&I loan yields in the last two weeks of Q3 and a better Q4 NIM tone, in line with management's 'steepening yield curve benefits our NIM outlook'. Against that sits an AOCI hit to tangible book value ($30.75 at Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior LKFN print turned on a rate move in this record. LKFN gives no numeric NIM guide, so the line surfaces only as call commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro and public, so largely priced. What is not priced is LKFN's own sensitivity, which it describes as a neutral rate posture with no table in the excerpts read. File it as a small macro-to-company proxy.
findings.independence: First Merchants Q3 2026 release notes rising rates hurt securities valuations (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000712534/000071253426000073/a3q26earningsreleaseex991.htm). The Fed decision itself rests on one secondary source; not verified on federalreserve.gov.

findings.finding: Expense growth is running ahead of revenue. Q2 2026 noninterest expense was +13% y/y against revenue +7%, and the efficiency ratio rose to 48.6% from 45.9%. Branch build-out continues: two Indianapolis branches in development and a Fort Wayne market headquarters plus branch at Electric Works announced 2026-10-07, opening H1 2027. Expense commentary on the call could weigh on the operating-leverage story.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 expense growth of +13% y/y did not stop a +3.67% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Expansion announcements are public; the cost per branch is not quantified anywhere, so the run-rate implication for 2027 is not in estimates. Small.
findings.independence: The Q2 release expense figures (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000721994/000072199426000063/lkfn-20260727exhibit991.htm) are a separate document from the Fort Wayne release.

findings.finding: Capital return is steady: the quarterly dividend was held at $0.52 on 2026-10-13 (unchanged from July; LKFN raises in January), and $17.1M of buyback authority remains through 2027-04-30. Share count was flat between 06-30 (24,858,875) and 07-29 (24,857,840), so there was no July buying.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dividend changes come in January (+4% in 2026-01). No reaction tied to buyback pace.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing unpriced: it is filed for completeness. Q3 buyback volume near the 52-week low ($58 area) would be a small positive and is unknown until the release.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The tape has the stock near its 52-week low with a negative 20-day run-up and short interest building to about 10% of shares, so a positive lean cuts against current positioning. It does fit the name's reaction history, which bought three of the last four beats.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy smaller than a company number): cut the peer NIM finding from +0.6 to +0.5. It is kept because a peer print after the company last spoke is the pattern the file says has paid.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): cut the credit-migration finding from -0.8 to -0.6, with 10% of shares short and 11 days to cover.
Lesson 5 (unconfirmed macro-to-company transmission): cut the Fed-hike/rate finding from +0.3 to +0.2.

Lessons 1 and 6 left the run-rate finding at +1.0. The bar is sourced to three agreeing estimates. The mixed reaction history (Q3 2025 beat sold -5.1%) was already in the draft size and in p_up 58. The impact sum and the scaled number are unchanged at +1.30 and +0.56.
